Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_averland}Averland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_averland}Averland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_averland}The Grand County of Averland is a major and founding Imperial Province that lies directly to the south-east of the Empire. Averland has an economy based mostly on agriculture, and the raising of cattle and livestock. Unlike most states in the Empire, Averland contains large stretches of unbroken open plains and while this land is not as fertile as those in Ostermark, it proved valuable as grazing grounds for the infamous Averlander cattle herds. Averland also has the 'honour' of defending the site of Black Fire Pass, which leads across the Worlds Edge Mountains from the Dark Lands. This is the clearest pass for thousands of miles and as such, is a popular route for marauding Orcs and Goblins. As a result of years of defending it, the Averlanders are held in high esteem in the art of siege defences.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_stirland}Stirland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_stirland}Stirland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_stirland}The Grand County of Stirland is a major and founding Imperial Province that lies within the eastern territories of the Empire. Stirland is a rugged highland province famous for its rural backwater society and the province's close affiliation with death. Such attitude stems from the province close association with the province of Sylvania, a land perpetrated with misty forests and ancient castles resting on the craggy peaks like circling vultures. Ever since the end of the Vampire Wars, the province of Stirland has been given the rights to all the lands of eastern Sylvania. This essentially doubled the size of the province, but did little to improve the province's fortunes. Indeed, the province of Stirland is a relatively poor country in comparison to its surrounding southern neighbours such as Averland or Wissenland. The citizenry of Stirland are a conservative and superstitious lot, known for their backwards outlook and religious intolerance. The Banner of Stirland shows a skeleton sounding a hunting horn, signifying a call to battle. The skeleton itself is a common symbol of the lands, an expression of both the Stirlander battle cry -Victory or Death- and a grim reminder of the lands of Sylvania that they share borders with.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_wissenland}Wissenland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_wissenland}Wissenland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_wissenland}The Grand County of Wissenland is a major and founding Imperial Province that lies at the most southern territories of the Empire. The province of Wissenland is considered the armory of the Empire, for it holds within its borders the city-state of Nuln, the largest industrial city within the Old World. From its workshops and factories, the city of Nuln churns out some of the most devastating black-powder weaponry known to Mankind. Wissenland's territories was originally confined between the Grey Mountains and the River Soll, but following the destruction of Solland in 1707 IC, the territories of Solland were given to Wissenland. Ever since then, the people of Wissenland have expressed a degree of sorrow and remembrance for their neighbors, going as far as to add the flag of Solland upon their own banners as a sign of respect for their fallen countrymen.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_talabecland}Talabecland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_talabecland}Talabecland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_talabecland}The Grand Duchy of Talabecland is a major and founding Imperial Province that is located in the geographic centre of the Empire. The province of Talabecland is perhaps one of the largest of the Imperial provinces, and its dominant features include its dominion over the River Stir and the River Talabec, as well political control over nearly all of the Great Forest. Much of the province's trade flows along these rivers, as well as trade that flows through to the north and south along the Great Forest Road.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_reikland}Reikland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_reikland}Reikland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_reikland}The Grand Principality of Reikland is a major and founding Imperial Province. It is located in the southwestern Empire in the centre of the Old World continent. Reikland has been the most important state of the Empire for nearly one hundred years, for it surrounds Altdorf, the current Imperial capital city, and its state armies are those under the command of the Emperor Karl Franz himself.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_middenland}Middenland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_middenland}Middenland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_middenland}Middenland, officially the Grand Duchies of Middenland and Middenheim, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that lies in the north-central region of that realm. Towering above the gloomy canopies of the Drakwald Forest is a sheer-sided pinnacle of white rock atop which sits the fortress city-state of Middenheim, capital of Middenland and the sacred City of the White Wolf. The White Wolf is the holy symbol of Ulric, the Imperial god of war, winter and wolves.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_ostenmark}Ostermark
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_ostenmark}Ostermark
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_ostenmark}Ostermark, officially the League of Ostermark, but sometimes called the East March, is an Electoral Province of the Empire that was formally founded only very late in Imperial history. It lies at the far north-eastern corner of the Empire.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_hochland}Hochland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_hochland}Hochland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_hochland}Hochland, officially the Grand Barony of Hochland, is one of the founding Electoral Provinces of the Empire. It lies between the northern provinces of Middenland, Ostland and the borders of Talabecland. Hochlanders are therefore known among the friendliest and most tolerant people of the Empire. Besides the Cities Hergig and Krudenwald, there is the untamed wilderness of forests and mountains and very limited ground for agriculture. The people of Hochland are famous for their love for guns and the best archers and marksmen regiments of the empire originate from this state. It is said that Hochlanders love their guns more than their wives.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_nordland}Nordland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_nordland}Nordland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_nordland}Nordland, officially the Grand Barony of Nordland, is an Electoral Province of the Empire that lies on the northwestern shores of that realm. Since its incorporation as a province, Nordland has become famous for hosting the Second Fleet of the Imperial Navy and its heavily tolled coastal roads, which provide both safe passage for rich merchants heading towards the city of Marienburg and the main source of income for its provincial government. Many sea fortresses and watch-towers line the coast of Nordland, as Norscan raiders from across the Sea of Claws are an all-too-common threat that can't be ignored without dire consequences.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_ostland}Ostland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_ostland}Ostland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_ostland}Ostland, formally the Grand Principality of Ostland, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that makes up much of the northern border of that nation. Ostland is a realm of damp, creeping mists and shifting shadows, and is covered almost entirely by the dark canopy of the Forest of Shadows. The people of this land have learned to live out a rugged life among the ancient trees, clearing patches of land for their farms and settlements, and keeping a watchful eye on the dark depths of the forest.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_brasskeep}Repugnauts of Brass Keep
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_brasskeep}Brass Keep
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_brasskeep}After the defiling of the Brass Keep in the Great War Against Chaos, the fortress became an oozing mess of slop and gushing mucus after the Nurgle worshippers asked the plaguefather to bless the fortresses foundations. After being cut off and surrounded the non Nurgle aligned warriors slowly fell to the diseases. Only the servants of Nurgle survived the gifts of plague, and they eventually became known as Putrid Blightkings.Now most of the band are trivial servants of chaos and aspiring warriors to Grandfather Nurgle, while they are led by the original survivors of the Fecund Fortress.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_wasteland}The Wasteland
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_wasteland}Wasteland
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_wasteland}The Wasteland, formerly the Electoral Province of the Empire of Man known as the Barony of Westerland, or just the Westerland, is the coastal region of moors and swamps that surrounds the mouth of the River Reik and is the homeland of the prosperous commercial city-state of Marienburg. The Wasteland was for centuries a part of the Empire, first conquered in 501 IC by Emperor Sigismund II, until the Westerland seceded during the reign of Emperor Dieter IV in 2429 IC by providing the emperor with a hefty bribe. Thereafter, the region is simply known as The Wasteland.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_moot}The Moot
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_moot}The Moot
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_moot}The Grand County of the Mootland, commonly referred to as The Moot, is a province of The Empire and homeland of the Halflings. Its capital is the town of Eicheschatten. Its symbol is a Fighting Cockerel and its colours are red and green.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_couronne}Dukedom of Couronne
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_couronne}Couronne
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_couronne}The Dukedom of Couronne is a founding dukedom of Bretonnia that lies upon the northern shores of that realm and is the current seat of power of the king's Royal Court, located in the dukedom, and the kingdom's capital, Castle Couronne.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_languille}Dukedom of L'Anguille
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_languille}L'Anguille
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_languille}L'Anguille, formally the Dukedom of L'Anguille, is a dukedom of Bretonnia that lies at the northern shores of that kingdom. Known far and wide for having some of the busiest ports in all of Bretonnia, L'Anguille is a rich dukedom that relies heavily on sea-trade for their fortunes. As such, there is a large number of merchants and middle-class commoners amongst the peasant population of the capital.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_lyonesse}Dukedom of Lyonesse
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_lyonesse}Lyonesse
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_lyonesse}Lyonesse, formally the Dukedom of Lyonesse, is one of the founding dukedoms of Bretonnia that lies upon the north-western shores of that kingdom. One of the larger dukedoms, the lands of Lyonesse are infamously known for their rivalry not with the other Bretonnian dukedoms, but amongst their own nobility, even in comparison to the feudal conflicts which plague the other realms of Bretonnia. People blame the unusual geography of the dukedom for the prevalence of the internecine strife, particularly the profusion of excellent sites for fortifications, which deters rival dukedoms from waging war or pursuing feuds with the lords of Lyonesse.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_artois}Dukedom of Artois
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_artois}Artois
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_artois}Artois, formally the Dukedom of Artois, is a founding dukedom of Bretonnia that lies at the heart of the northern lands of that kingdom. Unlike the lush meadows of Bretonnia's other dukedoms, Artois is famous for being the only dukedom that is covered entirely by forested wilderness, known by the Bretonnians as the Forest of Arden. Due to this, the dukedom is in a constant state of warfare against tribes of Beastmen that have made the forest their new dark home.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_giroseux}Dukedom of Gisoreux
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_giroseux}Gisoreux
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_giroseux}Gisoreux, formally the Dukedom of Gisoreux, is a founding dukedom of Bretonnia that lies within the treacherous slopes of the Pale Sisters and upon the low woodlands of the Forest of Arden. Unlike in other parts of Bretonnia, where much of the land is either one type of landscape and of one type of people, the diversity in geography of this Dukedom has also created a diversity in cultures and customs. Those living within the arable plains to the south contain the typical farmers and peasants that is universal within all the realms. To the east, the lands are filled with harsh woodlands, where a different people live life as expert trappers and wild woodsmen. Finally, to the north, those people that can eke out a living within the Pale Sisters are seasoned mountaineers who can brave harsh conditions. The Dukedom also contains the Gisoreux Gap, one of only three locations within the entire Grey Mountains that allow passage between Bretonnia and the Empire.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_parravon}Dukedom of Parravon
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_parravon}Parravon
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_parravon}Upon the southern reaches of the Grey Mountains lies the Bretonnian Dwelling of Parravon. Parravon controls one of the 3 routes leading directly into the Empire from the Grey Mountains, that being Grey Lady Pass. Due to the duchy being situated both at the base and in the Grey Mountains, the Parravoners have an affinity with the resident Pegasi that reside within the mountain tops. Indeed, Duke Cassyon de ‘Parravon has befriended the lord of all Pegasi, Glorfinal.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_montfort}Dukedom of Montfort
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_montfort}Montfort
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_montfort}North of the southern province of Parravon, and in the east of Bretonnia, the castles of Montfort reside. Like Parravon, the duchy of Montfort resides within the Grey mountains and below. Within Montfort lies one of the three passes into the Empire from the Grey Mountains, that being Axe Bite Pass. Being situated into the Mountainous regions, the Montfort peoples are hardy mountaineers themselves and due to constant raids, the Montfortians have developed a prejudice to any outsiders that are not Human, such as dwarfs, halflings, or elves.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_bastonne}Dukedom of Bastonne
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_bastonne}Bastonne
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_bastonne}At the very heart of Bretonnia lies the Duchy of Bastonne. Indeed located at the heart, but many believe that Bastonne is the Heart of Bretonnia. Founded by Gilles le Breton, the Cathedral for the Cult of the Lady is housed within Castle Bastonne’s walls. Indeed, just in the Forest of Chȃlons is said to be where Gilles and the Companions first met The Lady. Because Bastonne is the Heart of Bretonnia, the people of Bastonne are the most haughty and cocky of the Bretonnians. Bastonne holds in its service most of Bretonnia’s grail Knights, and rightly claims to be the most important of all Duchies.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_bordeleaux}Dukedom of Bordeleaux
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_bordeleaux}Bordeleaux
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_bordeleaux}The company kept by Duke Alberic is an interesting one. None but the most stalwart and talented knights are long permitted to fight alongside the Bordelen duke. As such, the men who are entrusted with the security of the realm are some of the most capable fighters, and outlandish nobles, in the whole of Bretonnia.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_carcasonne}Dukedom of Carcassonne
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_carcasonne}Carcassonne
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_carcasonne}A highly martial Dukedom, Carcassonne heavily focuses on militarization, and puts a heavy focus on the eradication of the Greenskin tribes in the Irrana mountains. Almost every person in Carcassonne, from the lowest of peasant to the highest of noble, is a warrior. Carcassonne has a strong bond to Brionne, due to the Carcassonne people’s fondness of poetry and music. They often remark with regards to Brionne that “We fight so the Brionnians don’t have to”

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_aquitaine}Dukedom of Aquitaine
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_aquitaine}Aquitaine
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_aquitaine}One of the founding dukedoms of Bretonnia, Aquitaine dwells on the western coast of Bretonnia, just south of Bordeleaux. Known for having some of the most serene lands in Bretonnia, Aquitaine is renowned for its cultivable farmlands and smooth sandy shores. Because of its isolation from many outside threats, much of the violence that occurs is in fact from petty squabbles between dukes, or peasant uprisings and revolts.Ruler Description: Inheriting the Duchy of Aquitaine after his elder brother had passed, Duke Armand d’ Aquitaine was the current standard bearer of Bretonnia, after his questing knight ventures led him to become a grail knight. After hearing the news of his brother's death, he was bidden by decree that he take the throne of Aquitaine. He now leads the duchy both as an administrator and as a Marshall.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_brionne}Dukedom of Brionne
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_brionne}Brionne
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_brionne}Brionne is often called the Jewel of Bretonnia… by Brionnians. It genuinely is a remarkably beautiful city, set on a peninsula linked to the mainland by a narrow neck. The peninsula forms a hill, and the city winds up the side, built with the local white stone or, for peasant buildings, white plaster. The sand of the bay is extremely good for making glass, so virtually every window inthe city is glazed, and they sparkle in the sunlight. Castle Brionne is at the centre of the city and the peak of the island. It is what other Brionnian castles want to be: the perfect merging of fanciful form and flawless functionality. The many small turrets might appear to be haphazard, but they provide excellent fields of fire. Similarly, the tall, slender towers hold watchposts that can be defended by one man against an army and command much of the area around. The many courtyard gardens can be sealed and turned into killing rooms to dispose of invaders. The Hall of Minstrels in Brionne is the most important centre for those entertainers in the world. It stands on a small prominence in the southern quarter of the city, and is surrounded by a garden. The building itself is circular, built of white stone, and home to an auditorium with flawless acoustics. Minstrels can be found performing there at any time of the day or night.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_quenelles}Dukedom of Quenelles
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_quenelles}Quenelles
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_quenelles}The people of Quenelles are fanatically dedicated to the complete destruction of Greenskins, particularly those who come down out of Massif Orcal to pillage their lands. Their questing knights are particularly renowned amongst the dwarfs, as many of them use their grail quest to venture into the mountains and badlands of the Old World. Despite this, the greenskins remain an ever present threat to the Dukedom, despite centuries of attempted extermination and colonisation of Massif Orcal. It remains a mystery as to why Quenelles suffers so much from the greenskins compared to their neighbours; some suspect that the descendents of Cuileux may have been cursed.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_sylvania}Sylvania
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_sylvania}Sylvania
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_sylvania}Sylvania is a dark and haunted region of the Old World. Though technically a part of the Imperial province of Stirland, it is in fact the independent domain of the Vampire Counts. Under the shadow of the Vampires, its populace has become a terrified, superstitious people. Close to uninhabitable, Sylvania's forests are dingy copses of twisted, half-rotted trees that claw what nourishment they can from the bone-strewn soil. Desolate moorlands and sluggish rivers of clotted blood punctuate the yellow-leafed woods, wind-swept and storm­ shrouded by dark clouds that seep down from the Worlds Edge Mountains on an almost daily basis.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_blooddragons}Order of the Blood Dragon
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_blooddragons}Blood Keep
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_blooddragons}Blood Keep was once the home of a valiant order of Knights known as the Order of the Blood Dragon, or the Ordo Draconis. One fateful night, a Vampire known as Walach Harkon challenged every Knight to single combat, eventually turning all who he deemed worthy into Vampires. The death of the Ordo Draconis was followed by their rebirth in blood; ever since then these terrifying warriors have been known as the Blood Dragons. The Imperials suffered under their attacks and depravations for sixty years, before they amassed a force to raze the Keep. That was almost six centuries ago, for all that time the ruins of the keep lay undisturbed. Now, the keep rises again, built by the silent undead, and the men of the Empire will again know fear.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_necrarchs}Scribes of the Grimoire Necronium
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_necrarchs}Tower of Shadows
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_necrarchs}Scribes of the Grimoire Necronium are dedicated to the study of The Grimoire Necronium, it is a powerful necromantic tome. It was created by W'soran, one of the first vampires and the only one to remain loyal to Nagash. In exchange, the arch-necromancer allowed W'soran to study his own tomes of sorcery, the Nine Books of Nagash. W'soran combined their lore with his own studies of the spirit realm and later, his apprentice Melkhior continued his work.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_mousillon}Dukedom of Mousillon
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_mousillon}Mousillon
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_mousillon}The dukedom of Mousillon is a haggard and dreaded land, full of swamps and cursed bogs. An impoverished land constantly plagued by disease, which many of its inhabitants have grown accustomed to. As such, many Mousillians are considered to be mutants and freaks compared to normal Bretonnian peasants. The villages and castles are at the point of collapse, while the nights are haunted by apparitions and vile beasts. Only fools and deadmen leave their homes at night.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_athelloren}Realms of Athel Loren
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_athelloren}Athel Loren
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_athelloren}Athel Loren the great forest of the old world is divided into twelve Asrai kingdoms, each ruled by ancient lord's and lady's of the great council. The flow of time works different in Athel Loren. Some realms are permanently locked in time and what seems like the passing of a season is actually years. Others dwell in an eternal night or in the glory of the light of the midday sun. The magical halls of elven lords and ladies are scattered throughout the glades of these kingdoms forming having their own identity and custom's. In these places, enveloped by a dim light, you can hear laughter and ghostly tunes that are reminiscent of the wind blowing through the spring branches. Its magnificent entrance portals are interwoven with the trunks of ancient trees or carved into the slopes of a hill. These places remain hidden from all those who are not welcomed by the Asrai. These beings may pass very close to these entrances, but they will never discover them.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_laurelorn}Wards of Laurelorn
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_laurelorn}Laurelorn
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_laurelorn}Once a proud colony of the Phoenix King, the Eonir of Laurelorn are the last remains of the High elves in the Old World, however, they assert their complete independence from Ulthuan after thousands of years of separation. In the Tragic events of the War of the Beards against the Dwarves, All colonies were either dissolved or burned down by the Dwarfs, leading to most of the remaining elves searching for shelter in the most northern province in Tor Lithanel. Though they called for support from the Phoenix Throne, Tor Lithanel did not receive any response and had a long-lasting fight for their survival as a result of these events, Laurelorn declared their independence. Today, the relationship between Ulthuan and Laurelorn has improved again. Yet, the Eonir do not believe anymore in the cause of the Asur. Instead, they arranged their situation in the middle of the empire of men.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_kadrin}Karak Kadrin
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_kadrin}Karak Kadrin
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_kadrin}Karak Kadrin, known in Khazalid as the “Hold of the Mountain Pass” is a proud and formidable Dwarf stronghold that watches over Peak Pass, a treacherous route that winds through the World’s Edge Mountains, linking the distant east to the Old World. Stood amidst jagged heights and snow-laden cliffs, the hold stands as both a bulwark and a beacon, renowned not only for its strength but also as the heart of the Slayer Cult. The Dwarfs of Karak Kadrin have long profited from their strategic position. With caravans from across the lands braving the perilous route to trade, the hold has grown into a bustling hub of commerce. Merchants gladly pay the tolls demanded by the gatewardens, knowing that within the reach of Dwarfen axes lies safety from the beasts and Greenskins that lurk beyond the torchlight. Yet for all its wealth, Karak Kadrin is no idle hold. The pass it guards serves as a corridor for more than just trade. Goblins, Orcs, and worse things still often descend from the eastern wastes, seeking to spill into the Old World. The Dwarfs, grim and resolute, man their outposts and bastions along the pass with iron discipline, ever ready to meet the foe and drive it back into the dark. What sets Karak Kadrin apart from other holds, however, is the solemn sanctuary it offers to the Slayers, those Dwarfs who have taken the Oath of the Slayer, seeking redemption in death against the greatest of foes. Within these halls, a Slayer may find shelter, sustenance, and camaraderie until he once more takes up the path of doom. While no price is demanded of him, those who linger often lend their axes to the defence of the hold, fighting alongside the king and his warriors to uphold their sacred vow to guard the pass. To fight beneath its banners is to walk the path of glory, or the path to the ancestors.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_angazhar}Karak Angazhar
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_angazhar}Karak Angazhar
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_angazhar}Karak Angazhar WIP.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_azgaraz}Karak Azgaraz
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_azgaraz}Karak Azgaraz
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_azgaraz}Karak Azgaraz is one of the major strongholds in the Grey Mountains. Though there are many Dwarf holds scattered across the range, none rival the majesty or wealth of those in the eastern realms. Karak Azgaraz stood long before the townships of the Empire were built, once enjoying rich seams of gold and silver. However, the more accessible veins have long since been mined out, and the hold now relies heavily on trade with the Empire to sustain itself. The King understands that for Karak Azgaraz to endure, new veins must be uncovered. As such, he frequently orders assaults upon the savage tribes infesting the surrounding wilderness, driving them back to clear the way for prospectors and mining parties. The hold’s survival, as ever, lies in stone, steel, and unyielding determination.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_eksfilaz}Karak Eksfilaz
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_eksfilaz}Karak Eksfilaz
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_eksfilaz}Karak Eksfilaz is a small hold situated in the far western reaches of the Vaults. Though not blessed with rich veins of gold or silver, the hold boasts an abundance of base ores, well-suited to the forging of weapons, armour, and tools of fine Dwarfen make. Karak Eksfilaz maintains various trade agreements with the men of the South, supplying many mercenary companies with Dwarfen-forged arms and armour to aid them in their endless wars.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_gantuk}Karak Gantuk
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_gantuk}Karak Gantuk
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_gantuk}Karak Gantuk sits nestled between Karak Hirn and Karak Angazhar. While Karak Hirn and Karak Angazhar enjoy trade with the Empire and are shielded from major threats from the south and east, Karak Gantuk has no such fortune due to its perilous positioning. As a result, the hold trades primarily with the Southern Realms and the occasional caravan from Barak Varr. In ages past, during the Time of Woes, Karak Gantuk bore witness to a great influx of refugees fleeing their fallen holds. These Dwarfs have since been fully integrated into the hold, yet their hearts still burn with the fire of loss, dreaming of the day they might reclaim that which was taken from them.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_hirn}Karak Hirn
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_hirn}Karak Hirn
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_hirn}Karak Hirn, known in Khazalid as the “Hornhold”, stands as the mightiest and most influential Dwarf stronghold in the Black Mountains, nestled between the northern reaches of the Border Princes and the southern boundaries of the Empire. Though comparatively young by Dwarfen reckoning, Karak Hirn has grown in stature and power, especially in the wake of the decline of the ancient Karaz Ankor. The hold's rise was slow and deliberate, built stone by stone in the shadow of adversity, and bolstered by the loyalty of numerous vassal clans and outlying settlements. Unlike many older holds, parts of Karak Hirn are carved openly into the mountain’s flanks, with some outposts exposed to the surface—an unusual feature in traditional Dwarf architecture, born of necessity rather than preference. Owing to its isolated location, the hold is not linked to the vast Underway network, forcing travellers and trade to brave the treacherous mountain passes and cliffside roads that wind perilously through the peaks. The mountains surrounding Karak Hirn are rich in iron and common metals, with smaller, hard-won seams of rarer ores and gems scattered throughout the depths. Yet it is not wealth alone that lends the Hornhold its renown.Karak Hirn earns its name from a vast cavern near the summit of the mountain, which produces an eerie, thunderous wail when the wind blows through it. This natural phenomenon has been masterfully harnessed by the Dwarfs. By constructing resonating chambers and massive iron gates that can be opened or sealed to control the airflow, they have fashioned a kind of natural war horn, one capable of shaking the very stones and striking dread into the hearts of any who would dare threaten the hold.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_izor}Karak Izor
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_izor}Karak Izor
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_izor}Karak Izor, known in Khazalid as the “Copper Hold” and called “Copper Mountain” by Humans, stands as the foremost and largest Dwarfhold beyond the World’s Edge Mountains. Its age, wealth, and enduring strength have made it a bastion of Dwarfen culture in the west. Dwarf settlements scattered throughout the Vaults and even as far as the eastern Irrana and northern Apuccini Mountains look to Karak Izor for leadership, protection, and kinship in times of strife. The mountain upon which the hold is built lies within the rugged expanse of the Vaults, a wild range where towering peaks, glacial cliffs, and deep, ice-hewn valleys mark the land. Here, the ancient rock yields generous veins of copper, iron, tin, and other useful ores, fuelling the forges of Karak Izor and making it one of the richest mining centres outside of the ancestral heartlands. Some of the oldest and deepest workings ever dug beyond the World’s Edge Mountains delve into these slopes, their tunnels echoing with the sound of pickaxes. Though the mountain itself is the heart of the hold, the influence of Karak Izor stretches far. In ages past, following the ruin of holds in the east, many Dwarf clans sought refuge here. Among them were remnants of the Dragonback Clan and the once-proud Clan Angrund. These exiled folk settled throughout the valleys, founding so-called “valley-kingdoms” beneath the shadows of the mountains. Though largely independent, these outposts remained culturally and spiritually tied to Karak Izor, looking to it as their ancestral anchor while they rebuilt, forged anew, and plotted the long road to reclamation. In the higher reaches, some daring Dwarf kings even carved homes within the glaciers themselves, stout halls of ice and stone, braced against the wind and time. Such places, though few, stand as testaments to the resilience and ingenuity of the Dawi. A handful of small, isolated human villages are permitted to farm in the more sheltered valleys below, but their presence is closely watched. Let none mistake it, the mountains belong to the Dwarfs. Every stone, every stream, every breath of wind that whispers through the peaks answers to the Copper Hold.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_kaferkammaz}Karak Kaferkammaz
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_kaferkammaz}Karak Kaferkammaz
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_kaferkammaz}Karak Kaferkammaz is a modest hold nestled tightly between karak Eksfilaz and Karak Izor. Because of its remote location, the hold only sees incursions from the underway, which is why the underway underneath Karak Kaferkammaz is still in good shape. The Dwarfs of Karak Kaferkammaz are very much aware of their proximity to the Wood Elves in the north and have had many reluctant dealings and border skirmishes with them, almost reaching a boiling point and leading to a war that neither could afford. King Skalf Redbeard was invited to the northern border by the Glade lords of Athel Loren a few centuries ago to negotiate, Skalf brought his own retinue of lords and thanes to the table. After many insults, threats and near fist fights, the meeting was interrupted by an ambushing force of Beastmen, who were waiting for the two groups to be distracted enough before striking. The battle was brief, the beastmen barely able to get close enough to the Dwarfen shield wall before they were felled by arrows, and those that did were swiftly cut down. As frustrations were vented during the attack the negotiations resumed and went much more amicably. Agreements were struck, pacts were sealed and the groups went their own way. Ever since, trade has flourished. Though centuries have passed, tensions are once again rising. The Wood Elves keep delivering shoddier wood, so the Dwarfs keep sending fewer shipments of metals.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_norn}Karak Norn
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_norn}Karak Norn
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_norn}Out of all the hills and mountains settled by the Dwarfs, the Grey Mountains are by far the poorest in minerals. The ore and gem deposits are also harder to mine because of the unstable bedrock. The Dwarfs who settled here were led by tales of untold riches underneath the earth, and their descendants cling to these tales with usual Dwarfen stubbornness, hoping to find these riches one day. Unfortunately, many years have passed, and more and more younger Dwarfs leave the Grey Mountains to seek their fortune elsewhere, the mood among those who remain is increasingly sombre and dour. The largest hold in the Grey Mountains is Karak Norn, Barren Earth Hold. Populated by displaced clans from several fallen holds such as Mount Silverspear and the watchtowers of Mad Dog Pass. Karak Norn sits on the only sizable deposit of ore and gemstones and is strategically placed with its upper level visible on a plateau high above the forest of Athel Loren. This allows the Dwarfs to monitor the activities of the Wood Elves, albeit from a considerable distance. While the Asrai haven't been a threat for over 4,000 years, and the grudge against the High Elves was officially settled with the taking of the Phoenix Crown at the end of the War of Vengeance, the Dwarfs see no harm in precautions. Karak Norn is the smallest of the main Dwarf holds outside the Worlds Edge Mountains, but it still has strong influence over the surrounding Dwarf settlements. The Grey Mountain Dwarfs enjoy a relatively peaceful co-existence with the Bretonnians to the west and a very uneasy truce with the Wood Elves of Athel Loren. They side with the Empire in times of war with Bretonnia, and have been known to close all major passes in the southern Grey Mountains, including the well-travelled Montdidier Pass that transverses the southern end of the range, near The Vaults.Karak Norn is defended by large Flame Cannons and powerful Bolt Throwers. Although clearly designed with the Wood Elves of Athel Loren in mind, the Dwarf defences are a formidable deterrent to any who might seek to invade their realm.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_zhufbar}Karak Zhufbar
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_zhufbar}Karak Zhufbar
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_zhufbar}Zhufbar houses the Dawi’s finest smiths and Engineers guilds in all of the Karaz Ankor. The surrounding lands house the superior metal known as Mithri- I mean Gromril, and is made into the finest crafts in the grand smiths in Zhufbar. Zhufbar is often looked down upon by many of the Longbeards and Greybeards for their innovation when it comes to gunpowder and technology. The Hold stands firm in the face of Greenskin raids, and Skaven incursions from beneath, as well as neighboring Sylvania. The hold is not open for any visitors from any nation besides that of its own, and honored Dawongr — trusted Dwarf Friends.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_karak_ziflin}Karak Ziflin
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_karak_ziflin}Karak Ziflin
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_karak_ziflin}Nestled within the Southern Grey Mountains, Karak Ziflin was a key chokepoint for the Dwarfs during the War of Vengeance.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_bad_axes}Bad Axes Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_bad_axes}Bad Axes Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_bad_axes}High in the Grey Mountains of Bretonnia the Tribe of Bad Axes roams. The Bad Axes are an unusual tribe for Greenskin as they ride Hagranyms into battle - A race of carnivorous horse-like beings. These animals are smarter than Greenskins and only allow themselves to be mounted as their Orc riders eventually ride down into bloody battles. The Bad Axes bear a grudge against the Dukedom of Couronne due to an event involving one of the past Royarchs and Gromodrak Hoofslasha, the current warboss of the Bad Axes Tribe.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_black_sunz}Black Sunz Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_black_sunz}Black Sunz Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_black_sunz}On the Western side of the Pale Sisters wanders the once mighty Black Sunz Tribe. Hailing originally from the plains of Zharr-Naggrund, led by the Black Ork Zorbak, these boyz migrated half the world to join up with the great Waaagh! that was supposed to destroy Ulthuan. Being late to the party, they ended up finding a scattered horde and found themselves quickly surrounded by the Brettonian humies. After a bloody last stand, the boyz were chased into the Pale Sisters and retreated inside the deep caves. Occasionally coming out of their stinky lairs raiding the lands of nearby Couronne and Gisoreux, the Orcs led by Zorbak are sure to make a comeback and return to their former strength.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_crooked_eye}Crooked Eye Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_crooked_eye}Crooked Eye Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_crooked_eye}Facing a fatal defeat against the Dawi-Zharr the Crooked Eye Tribe kicked out their former leader, Ruglud Bonechewer. After a heavy brawl over who should become the next Warboss. A victor appeared; it was Bazglud Daemonstompa. The mad lad had destroyed one of the Daemons sent by the Dawi-Zharr; he had made sure a part of the tribe could escape. Under this new leadership, the tribe restored its numbers and now makes itself ready to make Da Biggest Waaagh!

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_deff_grindaz}Deff Grindaz Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_deff_grindaz}Deff Grindaz Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_deff_grindaz}The Deff Grindaz is an Orc tribe north of Karak Norn, and east of Athel Loren. They are famous for the everlasting battle against their surrounding enemies. Waging war against the Wood Elves of Athel Loren, the Dwarfs of Karak Norn, and the Humans of Wissenland. They rule the southern part of the Grey Mountains. Capturing the old spoils of Gorbad Ironclaw’s Waaagh they became well supplied and an efficient enemy of the surrounding races.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_iron_tribe}Iron Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_iron_tribe}Iron Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_iron_tribe}Nearly 100 years ago, the enormous Waaagh! of Grom the Paunch swept through the Old World like a plague, ultimately meeting its end in Ulthuan by crashing upon the silver towers of Tor Yvresse. When the victorious Asur dispersed the Greenskin invaders, many severely weakened tribes sailed back to the Old World — The Iron Tribe being one of them. Now its hardy members are looking to replenish their numbers and raid neighboring humie kingdoms in true Greenskin fashion.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_massif_choppas}Massif Choppas Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_massif_choppas}Massif Choppas Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_massif_choppas}Greenskins of the Massif Choppas Tribe are the remnants of the once great hordes that had been scoured from the lands of Bretonnia during the founding of the kingdom. From their camp in the deep caves of the fortress known as Massif Orcal the Massif Choppas make themselves ready for the big Waaagh! that will make Bretonnia tremble once more.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_neck_snappers}Necksnappers Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_neck_snappers}Necksnappers Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_neck_snappers}Morglum Necksnapper is an infamous Black Orc Warboss who has led his mob from the desolate east to conquer many Orc and Goblin tribes in the World’s Edge Mountains. Those who fight hard enough (and survive) are allowed to join the Necksnappers Tribe, a still-growing horde that has achieved numerous victories. The Necksnappers Tribe is the most feared of the Black Orc tribes who have undertaken the arduous journey across the Dark Lands into the west.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_skull_smasherz}Skullsmasherz Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_skull_smasherz}Skullsmasherz Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_skull_smasherz}Known for terrorizing the Axe Bite Pass the Skullsmasherz are feared in both Bretonnia and the Empire. Reigning over the mountaintops and depths of the Grey Mountains, these Greenskins are a force to be reckoned with. Even feared among their own kind, the Skullsmasherz are one of the most, if not the most powerful, Greenskin clans in the west of the Old World.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_bloody_spearz}Bloody Spearz Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_bloody_spearz}Bloody Spearz Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_bloody_spearz}The Bloody Spearz Tribe is a clan of Night Goblins who ambush human and dwarfen caravans attempting to traverse the east provinces of the Empire near the Worlds Edge Mountains. Such is their wealth, it is said that other goblins, orcs, and even trolls flock to them seeking riches and war.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_red_eye}Red Eye Tribe
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_red_eye}Red Eye Tribe
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_red_eye}The Red Eye Tribe is a tribe of Night Goblins settled on the ancient dwarfen fortress of Karak Ungor. After the goblin occupation, it was renamed Red Eye Mountain. The greenskins stormed the dwarfen fortress by surprise from an underground route, driving the dwarfs out and taking over the fortress. Orcs were also involved in the assault, but they later abandoned the city, leaving the goblins of the Red Eye Tribe as sole owners of the hold. Today, Goblins of the Red Eye continue to be the owner of the place, ending the lives of up to 3 dwarf lords who wished to retake it.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_black_pit}Spider-Kult
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_black_pit}Spider-Kult
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_black_pit}When humans first entered the forests of Drakwald, they simultaneously pushed the goblins living there into the unknown depths of the forest, where other vile creatures such as Beastmen and enormous spiders already existed. Over time, these goblins learned to live with the spiders and even domesticated them for their own purposes. They used them as pets, mounts, food, or even to distill their poisons; and obviously, for war. From this relationship arose the Spider-Kult.

Kingdom.name: {=str_tor_kingdom_name_reavaz}Reavaz
Kingdom.title: {=str_tor_kingdom_title_reavaz}Reavaz
Kingdom.text: {=str_tor_kingdom_text_black_pit}When humans first entered the forests of Drakwald, they simultaneously pushed the goblins living there into the unknown depths of the forest, where other vile creatures such as Beastmen and enormous spiders already existed. Over time, these goblins learned to live with the spiders and even domesticated them for their own purposes. They used them as pets, mounts, food, or even to distill their poisons; and obviously, for war. From this relationship arose the Spider-Kult.
